summary_short: BioMarin's Q1 2026 revenue rose 2.8% y/y to $766.2M, but a $31.0M NAGLAZYME manufacturing charge cut gross margin to 74.5% from 79.7%; net income of $105.5M rebounded from a $46.6M loss in Q4 2025.
summary_long: Revenue grew 2.8% y/y to $766.2M despite a 12.4% q/q dip attributed to inconsistent timing of large government orders; VIMIZIM, NAGLAZYME, BRINEURA and VOXZOGO volume growth offset ALDURAZYME timing and ROCTAVIAN's voluntary Q1 withdrawal. Gross margin fell to 74.5% from 79.7% on a $31.0M NAGLAZYME manufacturing process-qualification charge. R&D rose on BMN 401 spend; SG&A rose on commercial expansion and Amicus pre-close costs. Net income was $105.5M ($0.54 diluted EPS), down 43.2% y/y but up from a $46.6M loss (-$0.24) in Q4 2025. Cash surged to $2,222M and long-term debt to $1,430M after February's $850M 2034 Notes issuance, pre-funding the April 2026 Amicus Therapeutics acquisition. No numeric FY2026 guidance was given in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: A steady quarter (revenue +2.8% y/y) was overshadowed by pre-funding for the Amicus Therapeutics acquisition, which closed in April 2026 after quarter-end and drove cash and debt sharply higher; a one-time NAGLAZYME charge compressed margins.
VIMIZIM/NAGLAZYME/BRINEURA/VOXZOGO grew on higher patient volume and government-order timing; offset by ALDURAZYME (Sanofi order timing) and ROCTAVIAN (voluntary Q1 2026 market withdrawal) declines.
Gross margin fell 5.2ppt y/y to 74.5% on a $31.0 million charge tied to an unsuccessful NAGLAZYME manufacturing process-qualification campaign.
R&D rose on higher BMN 401 spend and SG&A rose on Enzyme Therapies/VOXZOGO commercial expansion plus Amicus pre-close costs, outpacing revenue growth and the NAGLAZYME charge's drag on gross profit.
